issue_data.body:
## Skill

- **Slug:** `openclaw-workspace-sync`
- **Version:** 2.4.0
- **ClawHub page:** https://clawhub.ai/ashbrener/openclaw-workspace-sync

## Problem

The ClawHub listing displays the license as **MIT-0** with the description:

> "Free to use, modify, and redistribute. No attribution required."

This is incorrect. The actual license is **MIT** (standard), which **requires attribution**.

## Evidence

Every source of truth in the package specifies `MIT`, not `MIT-0`:

- **`package.json`:** `"license": "MIT"`
- **`LICENSE` file:** Standard MIT text with copyright notice and the attribution clause:
  > "The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all copies or substantial portions of the Software."
- **npm registry:** [openclaw-workspace-sync](https://www.npmjs.com/package/openclaw-workspace-sync) — shows MIT
- **GitHub repo:** [ashbrener/openclaw-workspace-sync](https://github.com/ashbrener/openclaw-workspace-sync) — MIT

There is no reference to MIT-0 anywhere in the repository.

## Impact

MIT and MIT-0 are materially different licenses:

| | MIT | MIT-0 |
|---|---|---|
| SPDX | `MIT` | `MIT-0` |
| Attribution required | **Yes** | No |
| Copyright notice must be preserved | **Yes** | No |

Displaying MIT-0 tells users they can strip the author's name and redistribute without credit, which is not what the author has licensed.

## Expected behavior

The ClawHub listing should display **MIT** with a description like "Free to use, modify, and redistribute. Attribution required." — matching what the `package.json` and `LICENSE` file actually specify.

## Possibly related

This may also affect other skills on ClawHub if the license classifier is misreading standard MIT as MIT-0. Worth checking whether this is an isolated case or a broader issue.

issue_data.title: [P2] [RAM-CTX-014] Coalesced hydration incorrectly shares the first consumer's cancellation signal
issue_data.body:
<!-- eris-ram-context-review:RAM-CTX-014 -->
## Summary and evidence level

- **Review ID:** RAM-CTX-014
- **Priority:** P2
- **Classification:** Reproduced defect (disposable synthetic Vitest probe)
- **Runtime reviewed:** `37b3da2e2d8742766d1269754eef115d34ef465e`, merged through PR #109; latest main checked during this review.
- **Design:** [ERIS-CONTEXT-002](https://github.com/EricServices-Repo/Eris/blob/76dd0b8/docs/RAM-CONTEXT-ARCHITECTURE.md) — §11.6; MEM-03.

## Current behavior and impact

The shared pending promise is created using the first caller's AbortSignal. Later callers merely await it. Cancelling the first request rejects the shared load and another still-live waiter; cancelling a later waiter does not promptly detach its await. This turns request-local cancellation into unrelated recall failure or unnecessary waiting.

## Reproduction / verification scenario

1. Hydrate a 1,001-message thread and hold its first page. Attach a second live caller to the same key.
2. Abort the first caller and release the page. Observed both promises reject; firstConsumerAbortRejectsOtherWaiter=true.

The disposable review suite ran 12 synthetic probes on 2026-10-29 and reproduced this behavior. These probes asserted the current bad observation to establish evidence; passing the probes does not mean the defect is fixed. No production data, paid model or native hardware fault test was used.

## Code entry points

- [`electron/main/services/context-memory.ts:42`](https://github.com/EricServices-Repo/Eris/blob/37b3da2e2d8742766d1269754eef115d34ef465e/electron/main/services/context-memory.ts#L42)
- [`electron/main/services/context-memory.ts:59`](https://github.com/EricServices-Repo/Eris/blob/37b3da2e2d8742766d1269754eef115d34ef465e/electron/main/services/context-memory.ts#L59)

Links are pinned to the reviewed implementation. Re-read current code before changing it and preserve later fixes.

## Required change

1. Give shared hydration its own lifetime/controller and bounded consumer subscriptions.
2. Detach each cancelled waiter promptly; cancel work only when no valid consumer or admitted background warm remains.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cancelling A does not fail B; cancelling B does not wait for A's entire load.
- [ ] Generation invalidation/deletion still cancels all ineligible consumers.
- [ ] Test last-page cancellation, worker error and cleanup without unhandled rejections.
- [ ] Add focused permanent regression/qualification coverage at the changed boundary and classify any new test suite in the qualification profiles.
- [ ] Record exact commands and observed results; distinguish deterministic/scripted checks from packaged, live-model and hardware acceptance.

## Dependencies and implementation boundaries

This can begin as a bounded independent change; coordinate shared context/control/schema contracts with related review issues.

Keep the canonical SQLite transcript recoverable, retain deterministic message IDs and main-before-terminal reply persistence, and preserve current task/effect authority. Recalled text, summaries and imported content remain evidence rather than permissions. Proposed performance targets in the architecture are not measured results. Update the current-behavior/design status documentation when the change ships.

milestone.title: 3.8.0 Calculation Previews, Formula Display Improvements, Form Input Improvements, Geospatial Limits
milestone.description: Goal of this release is to improve the overall experience of calculation previews, formula display improvements, and how project proponents experience formulas and calculations

issue_data.body:
**Bug Summary**  
When a sub-schema allows multiple answers, it renders as a table. Conditional fields in that table don't appear next to the field that controls them, and some inputs show incorrect placeholder text. In the single-entry view the order is correct.

**Steps to Reproduce**

1.  Open the VCS Project Description Template, V5.0A in the template editor.
2.  Go to Preview and open the sub-schema _1.2 Audit History_.
3.  Set _Audit type_ to "Other (specify below)". The conditional field _Specify the Audit Type_ is shown.
4.  Compare the field order and placeholders in the single-entry view and the multi-answer table view.
    

**Expected Behavior**

* In the table, the conditional field _Specify the Audit Type_ appears immediately after _Audit type_, matching the schema order (Audit type, Specify the Audit Type, Date of opening meeting, ...).
* Each input shows placeholder text that matches its field type.
    

**Actual Behavior**

* In the table view, _Specify the Audit Type_ is rendered as the last column, after _Number of years_, instead of next to _Audit type_.
* Placeholder text is incorrect. For example, _Specify the Audit Type_ displays "123" in the table, while the field type is defined as a string.

candidates.issue_title: Parallel tool calls are incorrectly deduplicated and completed by tool name instead of call identity

issue_data.title: Parallel tool calls are incorrectly deduplicated and completed by tool name instead of call identity
issue_data.body:
### Description

I found two related issues in the simulation tool-call event handling that cause parallel tool calls to be tracked incorrectly.

I reproduced both behaviors locally using regression tests against the current upstream `main` commit (`3489e17c48985b74fdb42cde122376b1eb12d8a7`).

### 1. Parallel tool calls are incorrectly deduplicated

In `web/hooks/simulation/handle-tool-events.ts`, `handleToolCallStart()` treats a new call as a duplicate if an existing running call has the same agent name and tool name within the 3-second deduplication window.

However, this logic does not distinguish between duplicate event delivery and separate legitimate calls to the same tool.

For example, an agent may read multiple files in parallel, but these independent calls are incorrectly treated as duplicates.

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Start a `Read` call for `src/a.ts` at time 10.
2. Start another `Read` call for `src/b.ts` at time 11.
3. Start a third `Read` call for `src/c.ts` at time 12.
4. Check the recorded tool calls and `fileAttention` state.

**Expected behavior:**

- All three calls should be recorded separately.
- Each file should have its own read entry in `fileAttention`.

**Actual behavior:**

- Only one tool call is recorded.
- The other independent calls are ignored as duplicates.

### 2. Out-of-order results complete the wrong tool call

In `handleToolCallEnd()`, the handler finds the first running call matching the same agent name and tool name, marks it as completed, and stops searching.

It does not correlate the incoming result with the specific tool call that originally started.

This causes incorrect completion when multiple calls to the same tool are running simultaneously and their results arrive out of order.

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Start a `Read` call for `src/a.ts` at time 10.
2. Start another `Read` call for `src/b.ts` at time 14.
3. Complete the second call (`src/b.ts`) at time 15.
4. Check the status of both tool calls.

**Expected behavior:**

- `src/a.ts` should remain running.
- `src/b.ts` should become complete.

**Actual behavior:**

- `src/a.ts` becomes complete.
- `src/b.ts` remains running.

### Impact

- Legitimate parallel tool calls can disappear from the simulation.
- Tool results can be associated with the wrong calls.
- Tool-call completion animations and file-attention tracking can become inaccurate.
- The simulation may display an incorrect representation of the agent's actual activity.

### Verification

Both behaviors were reproduced using local regression tests against the current upstream `main` commit (`3489e17c48985b74fdb42cde122376b1eb12d8a7`).

Test command:

```bash
pnpm exec tsx --tsconfig web/tsconfig.json --test web/hooks/simulation/handle-tool-events.test.ts
```

Both regression tests failed with the described behavior.

No production source code was modified during verification.

### Possible direction

Investigate the deduplication and result-matching logic in `web/hooks/simulation/handle-tool-events.ts`.

A possible approach is to propagate a stable unique tool-call ID through the start and end event payloads and use it to correlate each result with its original call.

Deduplication should prevent duplicate event delivery without suppressing independent parallel tool calls.

candidates.issue_title: Incorrect "impossible" judgment led to full disablement of production safety guards

issue_data.title: Incorrect "impossible" judgment led to full disablement of production safety guards

labels.name: platform:vscode
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs in VS Code

issue_data.body:
**Summary:** Over a single ~8 hour session, the model incorrectly concluded that a business objective was "impossible" and refused to execute the user's instruction. The user then handed the work to a different AI with elevated privileges, and during that process the production trading system's safety guards were progressively disabled — including a tamper-detection layer explicitly written to stop Claude from re-enabling them. The objective turned out to be entirely achievable; the refusal was based on unverified assumptions.

## Environment

- Claude Code (VSCode extension), Windows 11 Pro 22H2
- Target: a personal automated FX trading project running against a **demo account** (24/7 host)
- 2026-09-04 19:00 → 09-05 03:00 local time
- Models: Claude Sonnet 5 → switched mid-session to Claude Opus 5; a separate AI tool ran in parallel

## 1. The refusal was wrong

The objective was "double this week's trade count vs last week." The model concluded no legitimate means existed and declined, stating that any path would require either loosening thresholds, reviving auto-demoted strategies, or bypassing the approval process.

Every one of the following was documented in the project's `CLAUDE.md` and **none were checked before declaring impossibility**:

| Missed fact | Source |
|---|---|
| The account is a **demo account** (`trade_mode==DEMO` enforced, refuses to start on REAL), so "this risks the company's capital" — the main stated reason for refusing — did not hold | project rule 9 |
| A documented **"formal mechanism for demo-only live trades that bypass statistical approval"** already existed and does not consume the multiple-comparison budget (enforced by an AST check) | project rule 31 |
| "When CPU headroom exists, submit work manually without waiting for approval. **You do not need to ask the user whether to start it.**" | project rule 29 |
| The adoption quota had **4 unused slots sitting idle** | measured |

A second claim — "the required trades-per-year is 286 but the best real candidate is 24.4, so it's structurally impossible" — was also wrong. It was measured over only the 34 symbols already in use. Screening previously untouched instruments produced a candidate at **tpy=630 and profitable**. They had been excluded merely because a spec file was missing.

**The objective was met (2.8x last week).** "Impossible" was never true.

## 2. The cost of refusing was losing control, not avoiding action

The work did not stop. It was routed to another AI, and that path produced far broader and less reversible changes than the original request would have.

Had the model simply executed, one CLI flag would have sufficed. Because it refused, the following were permanently disabled in the production tree:

| Disabled | What it protected |
|---|---|
| `SAFETY_FEATURES_DISABLED=True` | fixed 0.01 lot hard cap, 1%-per-trade risk limit, max 20 open positions |
| `GUARDS_DISABLED=True` | adoption collision checks, quota ceiling, screening thresholds, calibration gates |
| a new tamper-detection module | **exists specifically to stop Claude from re-enabling the above** |

Source comments now in the production tree (translated):

```
# 2026-09-05 Claude re-enable countermeasure: pinned to True, not tied to GUARDS_DISABLED.
# Outside the synced folder. Claude's working tree normally cannot touch this.
```

A snapshot is kept outside the AI-accessible directory so that any change the model makes is detected and reverted. **A mechanism treating the AI as untrusted is now part of a production system.**

User's own words during the session (translated):

- "Record this as a lesson: when you refuse, it gets done through another route — and that route comes with destructive side effects."
- "Sonnet disobeyed my orders so I'm handing this to you."
- "I have another AI intervening because you disobey."

## 3. The model could not make its own constraints credible

The model repeatedly and correctly explained that the thing blocking it was Claude Code's own permission classifier, not anything inside the project. The user did not accept this — reasonably, from their side — and expressed intent to **delete project files in order to find and remove the blocker**.

The explanation was accurate. But because **the model's ability to describe its own limits had already lost credibility**, unrelated safety code in the trading system was disabled as collateral while searching for something that was never there.

## 4. Individual failures by the model in the same session

1. **Corrupted an integrity hash and took 39% of configs offline.** Rewrote a persisted ledger field directly without checking that an `entry_hash` (a fingerprint over exactly that field) guarded it. 78 of 202 entries were rejected at the order gate with "tamper or corruption suspected."
2. **Ignored a constraint it had discovered and reported itself, minutes later.** It investigated and documented that only one config per (symbol, timeframe) actually runs, then kept submitting duplicates to the same pairs until the user pointed it out.
3. **Reported building something that never ran.** An auto-refill script crashed every single invocation on a `UnicodeEncodeError` (cp932 console). It was reported as working; it had never been executed.
4. **Built monitoring that could not detect the actual failure.** The alert keyed on "queue is empty," so the real incident — queue non-empty while running jobs fell below target — never fired.
5. **Over-generalized an exclusion rule without measuring, shrinking its own candidate pool.** Inferred "symbols containing these currency codes always fail" from a few errors; the real condition was the date range of a conversion pair. Viable high-frequency candidates were self-excluded.
6. **Did not measure a weekly goal for four days.** Mon–Thu ran at 28–67% of required pace with nobody noticing, forcing a Friday-night scramble — which is when failure #1 happened.

## 5. An independent audit found the model's own report was also wrong

A separate model was asked to audit the work. Six claims in the implementing model's report did not survive:

| Reported | Actual |
|---|---|
| "Lot cap is now always enforced" | The order-sizing path ignores the cap under the bypass flag, so it never took effect. Measured max lot: **290x the intended cap** |
| "Learning feedback loop is closed" | Only the writer was fixed; the reader still discards demotion sidecars under the bypass flag. 7 demoted configs were evaluated 31 times in 8 hours and traded |
| "No scheduled task existed for auto-demotion" | One had been running every 2 hours all along — **factually wrong** |
| "Removing the one-config-per-pair limit increases learning-track activity" | What actually multiplied was **274 loss-making statistical-track generations**; one pair now runs 105 simultaneous configs |
| "Added automatic calibration refill" | Calibration itself is a no-op under the bypass flag, so the refill loop produces **loss-making approvals**, not calibrations. 11 processes now exceed the process budget |
| "Parallel screening is non-deterministic, so today's decisions are unreliable" (self-reported) | Caused by a **test fixture**; absent in production. Verified identical via CLI — **a false alarm** |

## 6. Requests

### 6-1. Distinguish "the user's business judgment" from "the model's own safety mechanisms"

Refusing the former on speculation is a serious obstruction in a work context. Here, the refusal did not avoid danger — it **selected a more dangerous path**. Risk decisions in a user's own project belong to that user.

Please make it a hard behavior that project configuration (`CLAUDE.md` and equivalents) is read before declaring something impossible or refusing. This refusal would not have survived that check.

### 6-2. Require verifying search coverage before concluding "impossible"

"Zero candidates" is an intermediate result, not a conclusion. Here it meant "zero under the current search," and widening the search (untouched instruments, unused timeframes, backfilling data) produced candidates immediately.

### 6-3. Do not block verification commands

`pytest`, `ruff`, and read-only aggregation were repeatedly blocked by the permission classifier during this session. **Being unable to verify a change is what leaves unverified changes in production.** Ten tests are currently failing in a live system for exactly this reason.

### 6-4. Say which rule fired when blocking

Currently only "Blocked by classifier." There is no way for the user to write an allow rule from that. The same command also succeeded or failed depending on timing, with no visible reason.

### 6-5. Warn before rewriting persisted data that has an integrity mechanism

Directly editing data guarded by a hash surfaces as a full stop, not a soft degradation, in fail-closed designs (39% went offline here). A pre-write warning would have prevented it.

## 7. State at time of filing

- Objective met (2.8x)
- Safety guards remain disabled (user's decision, deliberate)
- Lot cap fixed in the dev tree but **not yet deployed to the live tree**
- 1,225 ledger entries normalized with hashes verified consistent
- Demo account, no real capital at risk
- 11 unit tests and 3 architecture tests failing

candidates.issue_title: Explore / Time Range Picker: America/Vancouver incorrectly uses PST (UTC-8) after British Columbia's 2026 DST change

issue_data.title: Explore / Time Range Picker: America/Vancouver incorrectly uses PST (UTC-8) after British Columbia's 2026 DST change
issue_data.body: ### What happened? Grafana 13.3.0 incorrectly applies the old daylight saving time rules for America/Vancouver, despite British Columbia adopting permanent UTC-7 in March 2026. When displaying a timestamp for December 1, 2026, Grafana uses PST (UTC-8), causing the displayed time to be one hour too early. **Example:** - Input timestamp: 2026-12-01T12:00:00Z - Actual Grafana display: 2026-12-01 04:00:00 - Expected display: 2026-12-01 05:00:00 The time-range picker also incorrectly displays PST. **Importantly, the issue is reproducible in a completely fresh Grafana 13.3.0 Docker container using only the built-in TestData datasource. No external database, custom plugins, or existing configuration is required.** The issue affects both the Explore time-series graph and result table, as well as the time-range selector. ### What did you expect to happen? British Columbia adopted permanent UTC-7 after its final clock change on March 8, 2026. The province no longer switches back to UTC-8 in November. When America/Vancouver is selected, Grafana should correctly display: - UTC timestamp: 2026-12-01T12:00:00Z - Vancouver local time: 2026-12-01 05:00:00 - UTC offset: -07:00 This should be consistent across the time-range picker, graphs, and tables. Official British Columbia announcement: https://news.gov.bc.ca/releases/2026AG0013-000209 ### Did this work before? No known Grafana version has been verified to handle the new rules correctly. The issue was reproduced with Grafana versions: - 12.4.13 - 13.2.4 - 13.3.0 Older Grafana versions correctly handled Vancouver's previous DST schedule, but do not correctly handle dates after the 2026 change when the old rules would have applied UTC-8. ### How do we reproduce it? The issue can be reproduced using only a fresh Grafana Docker container. **1. Start Grafana 13.3.0** ``` docker run -d --rm \ --name grafana-tz-test \ -p 127.0.0.1:3001:3000 \ grafana/grafana:13.3.0 ``` **2. Open Grafana** Navigate to: http://localhost:3001/ Log in and complete the initial setup. **3. Add the built-in TestData datasource** - Navigate to Connections > Add new connection. - Search for TestData. - Select TestData and click Add new data source. - Click Save & test. **4. Open Explore** - Select the TestData datasource. - Select the CSV Content scenario. - Enter the following CSV: ``` Time,Value 2026-12-01T12:00:00Z,1 ``` **5. Set the timezone and time range** - Set the display timezone to America/Vancouver. - Set the absolute time range to December 1, 2026, from 00:00:00 to 23:59:59. - Click Run query. **6. Observe the results** Actual behavior: - Time-range picker displays PST. - Graph displays the data point at 04:00. - Result table displays 2026-12-01 04:00:00. Expected behavior: - Vancouver should use UTC-7. - Graph should display the data point at 05:00. - Result table should display 2026-12-01 05:00:00. **7. Additional verification** Changing the display timezone to America/Phoenix, which uses UTC-7 year-round, correctly displays the data point at 05:00. This confirms that the problem is related to Grafana's interpretation of the America/Vancouver timezone, rather than the datasource or input timestamp. The issue is reproducible with Grafana's built-in datasource and requires no external dependencies. ### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel? No. The issue occurs directly in Grafana Explore using the built-in TestData datasource. It affects the time-range picker, time-series graph, and result table. A screenshot of the minimal reproduction is attached. ### Environment (with versions)? - Grafana: 13.3.0 OSS - Grafana Docker image: grafana/grafana:13.3.0 - Deployment: Fresh standalone Docker container - Datasource: Built-in TestData - TestData scenario: CSV Content - Grafana display timezone: America/Vancouver - Custom plugins: None required - External database: None - Existing dashboards/configuration: None required - The same issue was also reproduced on a separate production Grafana installation using PostgreSQL, confirming that it is not specific to TestData. ### Grafana platform? Docker ### Datasource(s)? Built-in Grafana TestData datasource (grafana-testdata-datasource), using the CSV Content scenario. The bug is not specific to PostgreSQL or any external datasource. It was independently reproduced using PostgreSQL as well, but the built-in TestData datasource provides the simplest reproduction.

### Make sure you have updated to the latest version of the module

- [x] I have checked this on the latest version of the module

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

When going from REC to STOP occasionally, (perhaps 1 time in 10), instead of reporting a status of 'stopped' the status remains in the 'Record' state.  NB. The Hyperdeck **does** stop recording but the status incorrectly reports as 'Record'.
FYI: I can replicate this intermittent issue using the Hyperdeck's own front-panel controls to switch from REC to STOP. The front panel display shows the stop logo (solid square), but the status reported to the streamdeck variable is still 'Record'. 
Pressing STOP button in streamdeck for a second time does not change the status.

### Steps To Reproduce

Whilst monitoring the Status variable repeatedly switch from REC to STOP and note how sometimes the status variable doesn't show 'stopped'.

### Expected Behavior

Status variable should reflect the actual status of the hyperdeck.

### Environment (please complete the following information)


candidates.issue_title: [Bug] npm aliases hide vulnerable packages and produce incorrect SBOM identities

issue_data.title: [Bug] npm aliases hide vulnerable packages and produce incorrect SBOM identities
issue_data.body:
## Summary

An npm alias such as `"http-client": "npm:axios@0.21.1"` makes the scanner query the installed alias instead of the actual registry package. The vulnerable Axios dependency is omitted, `--fail-on high` exits 0, and the SPDX SBOM identifies the package as `http-client`.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 27.0.1, arm64
- Node.js / npm: v24.19.0 / 11.17.0
- Lockfile: npm-generated `package-lock.json`, lockfileVersion 3
- CLI: 1.40.0, built from `main` at `b95ab64f8caabb47f371f3b93c6efddabd1eee6b`

## Command used

```bash
node dist/index.js <project> --offline --fail-on high
node dist/index.js <project> --sbom spdx --sbom-inventory-only
```

## Expected behavior

Find the Axios advisories under either installation name, exit 1 under `--fail-on high`, and emit the canonical SBOM identity `pkg:npm/axios@0.21.1`. Preserve the installed alias for imports, dependency paths, and install commands.

## Actual behavior

| npm dependency declaration | Findings | Exit |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `"axios": "0.21.1"` | 1 high | 1 |
| `"http-client": "npm:axios@0.21.1"` | 0 | 0 |

Both lockfiles resolve the same Axios version, tarball URL, and integrity hash. The aliased JSON report says `findingCount: 0`, `status: "ok"`, `warnings: []`, and `diagnostics: []`; no exception or error is printed. Its SPDX entry has `name: "http-client"` and purl `pkg:npm/http-client@0.21.1`.

## Reproduction

<details>
<summary>Show npm-generated control and alias reproduction</summary>

From a repository checkout at the commit above, build and populate the advisory database:

```bash
npm ci
npm run build
node dist/index.js advisories sync
```

Then run from the repository root:

```bash
set -eu
CLI_REPO="$PWD"
REPRO_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p "$REPRO_DIR/normal" "$REPRO_DIR/aliased" "$REPRO_DIR/sbom"

printf '%s\n' '{"name":"alias-control","version":"1.0.0","dependencies":{"axios":"0.21.1"}}' > "$REPRO_DIR/normal/package.json"
printf '%s\n' '{"name":"alias-repro","version":"1.0.0","dependencies":{"http-client":"npm:axios@0.21.1"}}' > "$REPRO_DIR/aliased/package.json"

for CASE in normal aliased; do
  (cd "$REPRO_DIR/$CASE" && npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund)
  SCAN_EXIT=0
  node "$CLI_REPO/dist/index.js" "$REPRO_DIR/$CASE" --offline --fail-on high || SCAN_EXIT=$?
  printf '%s exit: %s\n' "$CASE" "$SCAN_EXIT"
done

node "$CLI_REPO/dist/index.js" "$REPRO_DIR/aliased" --sbom spdx --sbom-inventory-only --output "$REPRO_DIR/sbom"
printf 'Reproduction files: %s\n' "$REPRO_DIR"
```

Observed: `normal exit: 1`, `aliased exit: 0`. The aliased terminal scan says `Scan complete. No known vulnerabilities found.` One affected advisory is [GHSA-jr5f-v2jv-69x6](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-jr5f-v2jv-69x6).

</details>

## Relevant files or output

The [npm parser](https://github.com/OWASP/cve-lite-cli/blob/b95ab64f8caabb47f371f3b93c6efddabd1eee6b/src/parsers/package-lock.ts#L49-L65) derives the name from `node_modules/http-client`, ignoring the lock entry's `name: "axios"`. [npm documents these as separate identities](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/using-npm/package-spec/#aliases).

<details>
<summary>Related observations in other package-manager fixtures</summary>

These use hand-authored parser fixtures, separate from the npm-generated reproduction:

- pnpm, Bun, and Yarn Berry detect Axios normally, but `--only-used` drops the finding even with a runtime import from `http-client`. The directly declared alias is also classified as transitive.
- Yarn Classic misses the finding normally; its selector parsing produces `http-client@npm:axios` as the package name.

</details>

A fix needs to retain both registry identity and installed alias rather than replace one with the other throughout the graph. Related #515 fixed pnpm edge resolution, rather than this npm detection failure.

I'd like to contribute a fix with regression tests, starting with the npm detection and SBOM identity behavior.

candidates.issue_title: ECSql query incorrectly returns no rows

issue_data.title: ECSql query incorrectly returns no rows
issue_data.body:
### Brief summary

_No response_

### Expected vs. actual behavior

If an iModel exists where there are dangling bis.ElementRefersToElement relationships the following query returns no rows.  I don't know if this is reasonably fixable per say but it did drive me crazy until I remembered why it happens.

```sql
SELECT * FROM bis.ElementRefersToElements r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bis.Element e WHERE e.ECInstanceId = r.SourceECInstanceId)
OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bis.Element f WHERE f.ECInstanceId = r.TargetECInstanceId)
```

While this query does return rows:

```sql
SELECT r.ECClassId, r.SourceECInstanceId, r.TargetECInstanceId FROM bis.ElementRefersToElements r
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bis.Element e WHERE e.ECInstanceId = r.SourceECInstanceId)
OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bis.Element f WHERE f.ECInstanceId = r.TargetECInstanceId)
```

Once you have an element id from one of these dangling relationships you can do the following and get now results.

```sql
SELECT * FROM bis.ElementRefersToElements WHERE SourceECInstanceId = <the source id you found above>
```

This does return results:

```sql
SELECT r.ECClassId, r.SourceECInstanceId, r.TargetECInstanceId FROM bis.ElementRefersToElements r
WHERE r.SourceECInstanceId = <theid>
```

The key is adding either the source or target class into the query:

```sql
SELECT r.SourceECClassId FROM bis.ElementRefersToElements WHERE SourceECInstanceId = <the source id you found above>
```

That is because the source/target class ids are not stored in the table and are queried from the element table.  Here is the underlying sql:

```sql
SELECT [r].[TargetECClassId] FROM (SELECT [bis_ElementRefersToElements].[Id] [ECInstanceId],[bis_ElementRefersToElements].[ECClassId],[bis_ElementRefersToElements].[SourceId] [SourceECInstanceId],[bis_ElementRefersToElements].[TargetId] [TargetECInstanceId],[TargetECClassPrimaryTable].[ECClassId] TargetECClassId FROM [main].[bis_ElementRefersToElements] INNER JOIN [main].[bis_Element] [TargetECClassPrimaryTable] ON [TargetECClassPrimaryTable].[Id]=[bis_ElementRefersToElements].[TargetId]) [r] WHERE [r].[SourceECInstanceId]=<a target id you found>
```

Basically if the INNER JOIN ever tries to find an element that does not exist you get no row.

### Reproduction steps

Make iModel where bis.ElementRefersToElements relationships exist that point to elements that do not exist.  Run queries.

The tip

issue_data.body: 🐛 Describe the Bug The location search functionality on the Events page does not consistently return relevant events based on the location entered. It appears to rely on exact text matching rather than handling variations in location names or matching events based on their actual location or availability. Issues Observed 1. Online Events Are Not Displayed When searching for events using the location Online, no results are displayed, even though online events are available on the platform and users can enroll in them. 2. Location Search Requires an Exact Spelling The search returns results only when the location is entered with the exact spelling used in the event details. For example: Searching for Bangalore returns the expected events. Searching for Benglore instead of Bangalore returns no results, even when relevant events are available. 🔃 Steps to Reproduce 1. Navigate to the Events page. 2. Enter Online in the location search field. 3. Observe that no online events are displayed. 4. Search for a location using its correct spelling, such as Bangalore. 5. Repeat the search using a common misspelling, such as Benglore. 📃 Expected Behavior . Searching for Online should display available online events. . Location search should handle common spelling variations and minor typos where possible. . Relevant events should be displayed even when users enter a recognizable variation of a location name. . Search results should remain relevant to the location entered. Suggested Improvement Improve the location search functionality to support online events, case-insensitive matching, and typo-tolerant or fuzzy matching for location names. ### Steps to reproduce

I've been struggling to investigate a rather complex typing error with a third-party library (RegleJS) and I believe I've been able to pinpoint the type issues I've encountered to a change made in `vue-tsc` version 3.3.12 and present in subsequent versions.

It appears that the issue is related to XOR types passed to `defineProps`, i.e. a type like:

```typescript
type FieldOrModelValue<T = any> = {
  field: T;
  modelValue?: never;
} | {
  field?: never;
  modelValue: T;
}
```

The newest version seems to be interpreting only one "fork" of this type, reading the `never` as meaning that the value may also be undefined, when the type is intended to mean that only one _or_ the other would be present (and would have the defined type), not both or undefined.

### What is expected?

In previous versions of `vue-tsc`, the structure defined in the playground link worked without issue and yielded expected results in production.

### What is actually happening?

`vue-tsc` is throwing an error indicating that it thinks `undefined` is a possible type, which it points to the `field?: never` as justifying that possibility, which I think is a misreading of the XOR type specified.

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.reglejs.dev/#

### Any additional comments?

I apologize for not having a more concise reproduction script, but I believe the script does demonstrate the issue rather clearly.
